Dry run while paperTradeMode is on: every paper entry/exit of the main lane is queued as an intent and consumed on the next 5-minute cron; each is routed to the Polymarket US moneyline (league -> game -> long/short side) and priced on that book with its 0.0695 x p(1-p) fee; clobRef is the same intent on the global CLOB for comparison. Nothing is placed while dry. order = the FOK limit the executor would send (YES-price convention, tick-rounded, contracts). execPriceC = volume-weighted effective price for the paper size; slippageC = cents worse than the paper price; wouldReject = live rules that would refuse it (min size, slippage cap 5c, thin book); wouldBlock = the daily risk gates. routing.unroutable = intents with no Polymarket US market (the live path skips those trades). roundTrips diff buy+sell (both fees) against the paper ledger; dryMinusPaper is how much paper overstates. Maker mode (orderMode): a BUY rests post-only at the best level on our side (good-till-date = the TTL) instead of crossing; dry fills it when the market trades through the level or a print lands there, and at the TTL takes the taker fill (fallback) or skips; takerRef on a maker fill is the FOK it would have sent at placement, so maker.savedVsTakerUsd and roundTrips.makerMinusTakerOnFilled are the maker edge on the trades that filled; maker.missed are entries that never filled. Exits stay taker. Live: only with paperTradeMode off and PMUS_KEY_ID/PMUS_SECRET_KEY set; consumes the live exec queue, FOK limit or close-position with synchronous execution, confirms fills to the auto-trader, reconciles ambiguous sends against the account position and halts itself if that fails. POST /autotrader/executor/halt is the kill switch.

xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator). crosses = those minutes listed (newest first, with the US shares shown on the side taken; Kalshi sizes are not sampled) and whether each was still there on the next row (persisted): the Kalshi read lands a few seconds before the US read inside a minute, so a cross gone a minute later is most likely a book catching up between the two reads; one game carrying most of a sport's crosses points at a mis-mapped Kalshi leg.

usLane.read: Paper only: each event is a hypothetical taker fill on Polymarket US at the sampled quote (px, qty = shares shown at that price; one event per game minute, on the leg the US instrument quotes). tradable = the subset with at least 50 shares shown (usd = dollars on the shown size, capped at 1000 shares) in a minute where global Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c and the US quote was still crossable after the 6.950000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (edgeC = cents of edge at entry). marks.* = cents per share after the entry fee, marked at global Polymarket's mid 1/5/15/60 minutes later and at the end of the game (final), and at settlement (0/1); exit fees and the US spread are not charged on those. marks.x5 / marks.x15 are the round trip: closed on the Polymarket US book 5 / 15 minutes later (the bid for a buy, the ask for a sell, so the spread is paid) with the exit taker fee charged too - what a scalping lane would actually have booked. roiPct = avg mark pnl / avg entry price. noData = horizon passed with no sample. marks.kh0 / marks.kh1 are the Kalshi hedge (Oct 30 2026): the same leg sold on Kalshi at its bid (for a buy) or bought at its ask (for a sell) as a taker, priced in the event minute (kh0) or at the next sample (kh1, the honest one: the US leg first, Kalshi a minute later); the US entry fee and Kalshi's taker fee are charged and the position is then locked whatever the game does, so this is what a two-venue, US-legal lane would book per share (Kalshi sizes are not sampled; usd uses the US shown size; noData = Kalshi not quoted there). kalshiQuoted = the events with a kh1 mark, so kh1 can be read against x5 / settle on the same events (all and tradable), with the games carrying most of them (one game holding a third or more is a stale-quote artefact, not a lane). Decision rule (docs/PROFIT-AVENUES.md Part 2): after ~200 events, a Polymarket US lane is worth building only if the round trip (x5 or x15) is positive on the tradable subset with a hit rate above 50%, or settle is; a Kalshi-hedged lane only if kh1 is positive on the tradable subset at a hit rate above 50% over ~200 events with a Kalshi quote, and it beats x5; the real-money flip stays the operator's call.

scalp.read: The stale-quote scalp lane (src/scalp.js), two venues. Polymarket US (venue 'us', mode scalpMode): each minute the sampler sees global Polymarket's mid move 3c+ while the US quote has not followed and is still crossable after its taker fee, the lane takes the stale quote for up to $10 (never more than the shares shown, 50+ required) and closes on the US book 5 minutes later as a taker. Kalshi (venue 'kalshi', mode scalpKalshiMode, sports: NHL): the same minutes on Kalshi's own YES book for the leg, a stale ask bought as YES or a stale bid sold as YES (= buying NO), up to $10, closed on that book 5 minutes later; Kalshi sizes are not sampled, so dry assumes the quote holds for that size and live sends immediate-or-cancel orders that fill what is there or nothing. pnlC is cents a share after both of the venue's taker fees (Polymarket US 0.0695 x p(1-p), Kalshi 0.07 x p(1-p)), the number the paper lane's x5 mark reads for the US venue. Modes per venue: off / dry (decisions and fills at the sampled quotes, nothing sent) / live (real orders with that venue's key, only when it is on the worker: PMUS_* for Polymarket US, KALSHI_* for Kalshi). Risk: 3 open and 40 a day per venue, one stop at -$15 realized on the day across both, one scalp per game across venues, edge >= 1c; POST /xvenue/scalp/halt is the kill switch for both and the lane halts itself on an ambiguous send or an exit it cannot reconcile. byVenue splits the record. exitKind: x5 = closed at the hold on the venue's quote; late_last_quote / no_quote = no quote at the hold (dry), closed at the last quote seen or unpriced; x_live = the venue's fill (x_live_part = a partial Kalshi fill, the rest closed later); settling = the venue refused the close (market over), the position settles there and its P&L lands in the account balance, not here. The live flips are the owner's. probe (src/fill-probe.js, Nov 2 2026): every dry entry re-reads the venue's book a few seconds after the sampler's look (t0) and 10s later (t1); per venue, thereRate = the share of reads where the entry price was still quoted on our side, enoughRate = of those with sizes, the share with at least the scalp's size behind it, qtyMed = contracts left when it was there, goneAvgMoveC = how far the quote had moved against us when it was gone, avgS = seconds after the sample. This is the dry record's missing piece: whether the quote survives long enough for a live order to hit it.
